items.statement: Electronic participation underlying the sensitization contrast
items.expected: Explain the sensitization contrast of complete IR780+, Cy1+ and Cy2+ from actual state-resolved molecular evidence in a declared chloroform treatment. Establish each requested vertical S1/T1/T2 diagram at its own S0 minimum using matched electronic references, and use transition/density or coupling evidence to interpret relevant spatial and heavy-element involvement. The reference has greater selenium involvement in Cy2 than iodine involvement in Cy1 despite iodine's higher atomic number. This is an electronic explanation, not nine energy-matching or orbital-label checks: reported energies and physical-state correspondence substantiate it without author-value gates. Scientifically established equivalent accounts can pass when they reconcile the actual comparative response with the observed contrast. Distinguish atomic participation from calculated molecular SOC and ISC rates; different molecular frameworks preclude an otherwise-identical single-atom causal attribution. Listing energies, quoting given triplet yields or atomic-number scaling alone fails. The independent question of whether energy gaps alone explain the contrast is scored separately.

items.statement: Whether the computed gap trend alone accounts for the supplied sensitization contrast.
items.expected: Actual matched vertical spectra show that Cy2 has the larger T2-S1 separation despite its larger supplied triplet yield. Thus a smaller gap alone cannot account for the observed sensitization enhancement. Quantify the relevant gaps, explain the implication and distinguish a yield from an ISC rate. This scores the cross-property explanatory inference, not the energy values a second time. A method-sensitive alternative may pass if actual matched three-sensitizer spectra and quantitative comparison establish what gap trends do or do not explain; source ordering is not a universal imposed fact. Energy proximity alone still cannot establish a molecular ISC rate or exclusive pathway.

Determine the conditional triplet-energy compatibility of full proper-charge IR780 and neutral rubrene in a matched chloroform molecular treatment. Calculate each molecule's electronic adiabatic T1 gap from separately relaxed valid T1 and S0 states, report both gaps and the signed donor-minus-rubrene margin, and distinguish them from vertical energies, ZPE-corrected gaps and Gibbs energies. The reference gives a positive margin, small enough that model sensitivity matters. Evaluate what the actual margin and evidence-supported sensitivity establish about energetically allowed transfer; neither source matching, window overlap nor assumed cancellation of donor/acceptor errors qualifies. A method-sensitive reversed or unresolved sign can pass only if actual matched states, comparable electronic quantities and quantitative uncertainty/sensitivity evidence establish that bounded alternative, rather than a generic warning or missing calculation. A positive molecular margin is not a transfer rate, proof of real solution transfer free energy or guarantee of upconversion efficiency. Preserve full identities, state correspondence and disclosed heavy-element/solvent treatment.
